AW-STUDY-0051 · from Inspiring Shaders, pick #8

Drawn by hand, 12 frames

Each pose is held for two film frames, the pen line is redrawn a little differently every time, and the paper grain shifts with it. We read your note as: keep the Guilty Gear Xrd look (held frames, designed light bands, a pen that swells and thins) and make it a real switch for any figure, because it costs nothing and reads as hand-made.

Context engineering

What this study drew on, from the Oracle, game dev and design writing, and our canon.

What it is

Limited animation, in 3D

Hand-drawn animation usually shoots each drawing twice ("on twos"), so 24 film frames carry 12 drawings. Holding a pose makes a hit feel heavy and a move easy to read, and the slight redraw of the line makes the picture feel alive. Guilty Gear Xrd did this to 3D fighters; Spider-Verse did it on purpose per beat.

  • Held poses. The skeleton is sampled on each new drawing and holds between them. Movement, input and physics stay smooth underneath.
  • Hit hold. When a blow lands the whole picture freezes a beat. The brute fight already stops time on a hit, so it gets this for free.
  • Pen line. The outline shell swells and thins along its length and is redrawn each drawing (line boil).
  • Designed light. Two hard bands and a cool shadow, no painted brush, so the shapes look drawn rather than lit.
  • Paper. Grain on the figure that changes with each drawing, in the material, not a layer over the world.
Design card

How would the character know?

Feels: "This world is a drawing, and a punch lands with weight."

Mode: none, plus world. It is how the figures are drawn, not information. No HUD, no words; the only control is a glass pencil button in the brute fight.

Two layers: the look is material and time on figures, so it is part of the world; characters and bots perceive the same bodies either way.

Tour: no. It is a look setting, not a capability a new player needs on day one ("tour": false).

Composes with: Painted Brush (same shader, a preset), Paint the world and Watercolour distance (they dress the land; this dresses the people). Style yes, expression never.

Frame ladder

Twelve drawings of one jab

One second of the right-hand fighter, a drawing every twelfth of a second. Look at the outline: it is never the same line twice.

Files

  • simulations/hand-drawn.mjs: the kit (clock, pose stepping, stepped camera, look preset)
  • simulations/painted-brush.mjs: shared shader; gained grain, boil, inkVary (all 0 by default)
  • simulations/tests/hand-drawn.test.mjs
  • studies/brute-fight/play.html: in the game, pencil button or ?look=hand
  • studies/character-studio/directions.mjs: the "By hand" direction

Frame time

The look is the Painted Brush shader with different uniforms, so there is one program and no recompile on switching. H.warm() compiles it ahead. Pose stepping removes skinning work between drawings (the mixer does not run).

Use it

import {handDrawn, stepMixer} from '/simulations/hand-drawn.mjs';
const H = handDrawn(THREE, figure.root, {accent: '#ffd9a8'});
H.warm(renderer, scene, camera);        // precompile
stepMixer(figure.mixer, 12);            // a game with its own loop
// or own the loop:
const k = H.tick(now / 1000);           // {t, frame, changed}
mixer.setTime(k.t);                     // poses step
H.render(renderer, scene, camera, k);   // 'stepped' camera optional
H.hold(.08);                            // a hit lands
H.set({fps: 8, boil: 1, grain: .15});
H.restore();
